newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa has no record of alleged missile attack.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa has no record of alleged missile attack.

text.p: German airline Lufthansa AG said on Tuesday it had no record of an Indian air force missile which was allegedly fired at a Lufthansa Boeing 747 flying over India on January 15, as reported in the Pakistani press.
But Lufthansa said the report would be investigated.
It was attributed to The Nation newspaper and carried by the Associated Press of Pakistan on Tuesday, and said the Lufthansa jet had a "hair-raising escape" while in Indian air space.
A Lufthansa spokesman said the carrier had no indication of a missile attack on LH Flight 778 from Frankfurt to Singapore and that the flight was "absolutely normal".
"We have no record of any disturbance," said Lufthansa spokesman Christian Klick. He also said the pilots did not file a report of an unusual incident, required under company policy.
He said the press reports would be investigated in addition to an incident on January 11 when a Lufthansa jet reported a near-miss with an unidentified aircraft over northern India.
The Pakistani news agency quoted The Nation as saying an Indian air force Mig-21 had fired a missile at the flight 778 Lufthansa aircraft but had missed.
The Indian jet fighter later made visual contact with the aircraft and discovered the target had been a Lufthansa jet, the report continued.

Also on January 15, the day of the alleged missile attack, United News of India news agency said Indian air force planes had fired at a small, pilotless aircraft which had crossed into the Indian state of Gujarat from Pakistan.

India, which has fought three wars against Pakistan since the two states were carved out of British India in 1947, lodged a strong protest with Pakistan and said a remote-controlled aircraft had made several intrusions into Indian air space.
Pakistan has denied any such intrusions.
